method: Reviewed the full lesson, metadata/source registrations, DATA ledger, and existing dated review. Re-ran the 11-check offline verifier and independently recomputed all eight differences, paired and independent-sample standard errors, and exact sign-test tails. Opened the official NIST paired-observation, sign-test, and DOE handbook pages. No provider calls were made by local verification.

observations.trace: The statistical derivations and task-ID alignment were consistent: differences [37, 39, 1297, 307, 37, -202, -534, 837], mean +227.25, paired SE 206.765, independent-sample SE 248.636, and two-sided sign-test p=74/256=0.2890625. A fresh run exposed that these historical figures were missing from docs/DATA.md; the ledger now records the arithmetic-only results and unavailable raw evidence. NIST's paired-observation definition and sign-test treatment of ties and binomial signs align with the lesson's bounded claims. Source review is not a model rerun.

limitations: The original per-call prompts and responses, endpoint/model fingerprint, complete usage, scorer source, task-run mapping, and run order are unavailable; the historical measurements remain independently unreproducible.
The displayed values support arithmetic over the retained summary only. They do not establish quality equivalence, billed cost changes, a causal prompt effect, or population-level model behavior.

The sign test's inferential interpretation depends on independent paired units and balanced signs under the null; the eight historical tasks cannot be confirmed to satisfy those assumptions or represent a target workload.
